proposal_title: Add a reproducible WSL filesystem performance benchmark specification
verification_strategy: 1. Pre-flight ground truth: confirm pos/ exists, pos/package.json exists, pos/docs/ does NOT exist, root docs/ does NOT exist. Proposal must create the docs/operations/ tree; the file path is the only added path, but the directory is new.

2. Package-script fidelity gate: extract every script the runbook references and cross-check against the verified script set in pos/package.json (dev, build, start, lint, test, beads:project, beads:check, beads:next). Any workload whose script is missing MUST appear as an explicit blocker, not as an invented command. Expected blockers on this repo: 'development-server readiness' has no dedicated script (only `dev`); 'hot reload' has no dedicated script; 'dependency install' has no `install` / `ci` script (must use a direct command whose prereqs are documented).

3. No-premature-claim gate: run a grep for `linux.native (is|will|should) (be )?(faster|win|better|superior)|drvfs (is|will|should) (be )?(slower|worse|inferior)` and require zero matches. Direction-agnostic language only.

4. Decision-threshold predeclaration gate: locate the threshold section in the runbook and confirm it appears before any results / data-entry template, names the median-improvement rule, names the variability/confidence rule, and lists the three outcomes (relocate, do-not-relocate, collect-more-evidence or inconclusive). A single favorable run MUST NOT decide relocation.

5. Cold/warm cache gate: verify the runbook defines what may be cleared per phase, requires at least three runs per condition, requires run-order randomization or alternation, and requires median plus variance / spread. Cold-cache and warm-cache phases must be operationally distinct (not just relabelled).

6. Data-safety gate: confirm the runbook explicitly prohibits copying pos/.env.local, NEXTAUTH_SECRET, MONGODB_URI, and any active MongoDB state into temporary worktrees. The pos/.gitignore already excludes .env* (verified), so a clean worktree is safe by default — the runbook should state this so the operator does not undo it.

7. Scope gate: confirm the runbook does not propose installing dependencies, running the benchmark, deleting caches, creating branches / worktrees / PRs, or relocating the repository. Every destructive step is approval-gated and separate from the document itself.

8. Auditability gate: confirm result tables include workload, cache condition, run index, raw seconds, median, spread, env metadata hash, and a failure / notes field. Command lines and revisions must be retained without embedded secrets.

9. Paired-condition gate: confirm the runbook names BOTH conditions explicitly (Linux-native WSL path AND drvfs /mnt/<drive>/path), names a path example for each that is clearly a placeholder, and states equivalence requirements (same revision, same Node.js / npm, same env vars minus path-specific values, clean install / build state).

10. Runbook-reproducibility gate: an independent reviewer must be able to execute the runbook end-to-end from the document alone. Verify that prerequisites (Node version, WSL version, free disk, no concurrent heavy load) are explicit and that a warm-up policy plus invalidation criteria are present.

manual_review_checks: Ground-truth script map: confirm the workload list — dependency install, production build, test execution, dev-server readiness, hot reload — each names either a verified npm script from pos/package.json (dev / build / start / lint / test / beads:project / beads:check / beads:next) OR an explicit direct command (e.g. `npm ci` for install) with documented prereqs, OR a Blocker marker. Any item silently assumed is a fail.

Decision threshold placement: open the doc and visually confirm the threshold section appears BEFORE the data-entry / results tables. If it appears after, the runbook is vulnerable to threshold-shopping. Confirm the three named outcomes (relocate / do-not-relocate / collect-more-evidence or inconclusive).

Equivalence rules: confirm the runbook requires the same commit SHA or revision identifier in both worktrees (not just 'latest'), same Node.js major.minor, same npm version, same package-lock.json, and same env vars minus path-specific values. A subtle difference (e.g. dev-only vs prod NODE_ENV) can bias results.

No-premature-claim language audit: read the entire document and confirm no sentence asserts that Linux-native storage is faster, that drvfs is slower, that the operator should relocate, or that a relocation is justified. The runbook must be measurement-agnostic until results exist.

Data-safety wording: confirm the runbook states (a) secrets in pos/.env.local MUST NOT be copied to temp worktrees, (b) any temporary worktree must use disposable / synthetic config, (c) the active MongoDB / production DB MUST NOT be touched, (d) cleanup is reversible or approval-gated, (e) backups precede any destructive cache cleanup. The pos/.gitignore already excludes .env* (verified), so a clean worktree created via standard tooling is safe by default — the runbook should call this out so the operator does not undo it.

Worktree creation gating: confirm any instruction to create worktrees, branches, or additional copies of the repo is preceded by 'requires explicit operator approval' or equivalent. The runbook under this proposal must NOT itself create worktrees.

Cold-cache vs warm-cache operationally distinct: confirm cold-cache runs actually clear node_modules / .next / npm cache and require reinstall + rebuild, while warm-cache runs reuse the populated caches. The two phases must not collapse into the same procedure.

Run-order randomization: confirm the runbook requires alternation (ABABAB) or randomization between conditions so that a hot-then-cold host state does not bias the late condition. Counterbalancing matters more than number of runs.

Invalidation criteria: confirm the runbook defines when a run must be thrown out (throttling, OOM, background activity, dev-server port already in use, interrupted build). A 'degraded' annotation must be distinct from a hard invalidation.

Review-checklist truncation: the proposal's review_checklist ends mid-sentence at 'Results can be audited from recorded commands, revisions, metadata,' — the implementer should be told to treat the truncated bullet as 'recorded commands, revisions, metadata, and raw timings sufficient to reconstruct the median and variance from the run receipt alone.'

Path placeholder safety: confirm the example paths the runbook uses (e.g. /home/<user>/nexplay-wsl-native and /mnt/c/Users/<user>/nexplay-drvfs) are clearly placeholders and do not match real user paths on this host. The implementer should use $HOME-relative or ${WSL_NATIVE_PATH}/${DRVFS_PATH} variables rather than hard-coding /home/morderith.

One-file scope discipline: confirm the proposal changes EXACTLY one file — docs/operations/wsl-nextjs-filesystem-benchmark.md. No edits to pos/package.json, AGENTS.md, .gitignore, pos/.env.local, the existing pos/bench_results.txt, or any other file. The repo currently has no docs/ tree at the root, so creating docs/operations/ is the only net directory addition.
Cross-spoke hygiene: confirm the runbook does not invoke skills, beads, or paths from other Corvus spokes (moonshot, securesphere, taliesin, etc.). It is a nexplaynexus-local spec.
regression_risks: Documentation-creation side effect: this proposal creates a new docs/operations/ tree at the repo root. If the implementer is sloppy they could (a) also edit existing pos/docs/-equivalent files (there are none — verified — but they could create pos/docs/ by accident), (b) modify AGENTS.md, tasks.md, memory.md, or wireframe.md to mention the new spec (the proposal does not authorize these edits; the nexplaynexus AGENTS.md mandates a Preservation Principle — adding docs is fine, mutating existing memory/bead files is not in scope), (c) commit a draft that references scripts not in pos/package.json, silently propagating fabricated commands.

Premature-performance-claim drift: even a single phrase like 'Linux-native storage is typically faster' is enough to bias the operator's interpretation of later results. Grep must return zero matches for the premature-claim regex; the implementer must use direction-neutral phrasing throughout.

Threshold-shopping risk: if the decision-threshold section is positioned after the results template, the operator can move the threshold to fit the data. This is a structural regression of the runbook's scientific value. The placement must be enforced.

Secret-leak risk via copy-paste of the dev environment: a naive 'clone the repo' instruction can drag pos/.env.local into a temp worktree if the operator uses `cp -a` instead of `git worktree add`. The runbook must require `git worktree add` (which honors .gitignore) and must explicitly forbid copying .env* files.

Active-MongoDB risk: the repo has a live mongodb client (lib/mongodb-client.ts) and migrate / repair scripts. A worktree started while the dev server is running against the production DB can lock, write, or read live data. The runbook must state that the dev server is not running during measurement and that no script that mutates MongoDB state runs against the production URI.

NextAuth / POS-B002 cross-pollution: the standing memory note flags POS-B002 (NEXTAUTH_SECRET unsafe auth fallback) as P0. The runbook should not propose any auth change, but a careless implementer might add a 're-run npm run dev to verify auth' step that exercises the live auth path. Auth-touching steps must be out of scope.

Cache invalidation risk on /mnt: a Windows drvfs filesystem caches differently than the Linux-native ext4 / NVMe path. Clearing Linux page cache (echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches) inside WSL does not invalidate Windows-side file caching for the drvfs mount. The runbook must define how Windows-side caching is handled (e.g. by closing the file handles and waiting) or note that the cold-cache condition for drvfs is approximate.

node_modules size: a fresh `npm ci` for this repo pulls heavy deps (next, mongodb, recharts, framer-motion, xlsx, etc.). The runbook must state disk-space prerequisites and warn that the dependency-install workload is the most likely to be dominated by network rather than filesystem speed — this can mask the filesystem signal the runbook is trying to measure.

Power/thermal confound: the test suite (jest) and the production build both produce sustained CPU load. On a laptop without a power profile pinned, the first run can be throttled. The runbook must define a warm-up phase and a power-policy gate; otherwise the median is biased by the first run.

TS / lint long-tail: `lint` and `beads:check` may be I/O-bound or may be CPU-bound depending on the workload. Mixing them into the filesystem benchmark can blur the signal. The runbook should call out which workloads are filesystem-dominated and which are CPU-dominated.

Stale review_checklist: the proposal's review_checklist is truncated mid-sentence. If the implementer copies the checklist verbatim into the new runbook as a self-audit section, the runbook inherits the truncation. The implementer must complete the final bullet before using it.

Bead / memory coupling: the nexplaynexus AGENTS.md mandates updating wireframe.md, .agent/memory.md, .agent/beads/ledger.json, and tasks.md for UI changes. This proposal is NOT a UI change and is purely a docs addition, so the bead/memory update obligations should NOT fire — but the implementer should confirm with the .agent/beads/ledger.json before declaring the bead done.

(a) Exactly one file is created: docs/operations/wsl-nextjs-filesystem-benchmark.md at the repo root. No edits to pos/, AGENTS.md, memory.md, tasks.md, wireframe.md, .agent/, .gitignore, or any existing file. Enforce via `git -C /home/morderith/Corvus/NexplayNexus status --porcelain` showing only that path as added.

(b) The runbook contains the required sections in order: Scope, Non-Goals, Operator Approval Boundary, Prerequisites, Experimental Design (paired worktrees), Cold-Cache Protocol, Warm-Cache Protocol, Workloads, Environmental & Thermal Controls, Data-Safety & Secrets, Cleanup, Decision Threshold, Run-Receipt Templates, Blockers, Decision Criteria. Section presence is verified by `grep -nE '^## |^### ' <file>`.

(c) Every workload (dependency install, production build, test execution, dev-server readiness, hot reload) is either (i) bound to a real script in pos/package.json — verified by the per-script check above — or (ii) bound to a documented direct command with prereqs, or (iii) explicitly marked as a Blocker. Zero invented commands.
(d) The premature-claim grep returns zero matches. No sentence asserts that Linux-native storage is faster, that drvfs is slower, or that relocation is justified before measurements exist.

(e) The decision-threshold section appears BEFORE the data-entry / results templates. The threshold names a median-improvement rule, a variability / confidence rule, and the three outcomes (relocate / do-not-relocate / collect-more-evidence or inconclusive).

(f) Cold-cache and warm-cache protocols are operationally distinct: cold-cache clears node_modules, .next, and npm cache and rebuilds; warm-cache reuses the populated caches. Each condition requires at least three runs, with run-order alternation or randomization, and produces median + variance / spread.

(g) The runbook names both conditions explicitly: a Linux-native WSL path (placeholder, e.g. ${WSL_NATIVE_PATH}/nexplay-worktree) AND a drvfs /mnt/<drive>/ path (placeholder, e.g. ${DRVFS_PATH}/nexplay-worktree). It does not hard-code /home/morderith or any specific user path.

(h) The data-safety section explicitly prohibits copying pos/.env.local, NEXTAUTH_SECRET, MONGODB_URI, and any active MongoDB state into temporary worktrees; requires disposable / synthetic config in temp worktrees; requires backups before any destructive cache cleanup; requires graceful process termination; and requires temporary worktree removal only after results are captured and after operator approval.
(i) No PR, branch, worktree, dependency install, benchmark run, cache deletion, or repository relocation is performed as part of this proposal. The runbook is a document only.
(j) The runbook is at least ~4 KB / ~80 lines of substantive content (a stub that satisfies the grep gates but lacks protocol detail must be rejected).

REJECT if any of (a)–(j) fails. Common rejection causes to pre-screen for: invented `npm run` scripts, threshold section placed after results table, no warm-up policy, no Windows-side cache handling for drvfs, hard-coded user paths, single-run decision rule, secret/DB exclusions missing, premature performance claim, scope creep into existing files.
